messages:
Kai: Repro steps for the OOM regression after we flipped the kernel selector. It shows up on AWQ-65B with long contexts (~8k) when kv cache is fp16. Minimal repro below.

Rachel: Drop the exact run command? I'll spin it up on A100.

Kai: Run:
```
EXPORT REDWOOD_DEBUG=1
python -m runner --model awq-65b --seq 8192 --batch 4 --kv-dtype fp16 --kernel-policy latest
```
Logs have repeated "realloc fallback" and many "deferred_free window" warnings.

Sam: Allocator trace I captured:
```
[allocator] try_alloc workspace=512MB -> slabpool miss
[allocator] device_malloc fallback; enqueued deferred_free
[kernel] chosen=flash_attn_v2 (seq=8192)
OOM after 3rd request: live=18.6GB reserved=1.2GB free_fragments: 5x128MB
```

Leo: Sounds like the new tiered allocator + batch-steering isn't preserving kv soft-reserve across kernel variants. fp16 reduces persistent kv but increases number of small transient buffers -> more fragmentation.

Sree: Two notes: 1) AWQ params int8, but KV kept fp16; the cast path allocs a tiny temp per layer which aggregates on long ctx. 2) New kernel variant uses bigger transient workspace at >4096, multiplying working set.

Kai: Combined effect: reduced permanent footprint but larger transient workspace -> deferred frees can't compact fast enough and fragmentation spikes.

Rachel: Short-term mitigation: force kv dtype to bf16 and use conservative kernel policy: `--kernel-policy conservative --kv-dtype bf16`.

Sam: Tried bf16 locally: no OOM, but p99 up ~12% and token cost +4%. Ok for canary.

Leo: Longer term fixes:
- allocator: add an eager compaction path to coalesce deferred_free spans when fragmentation > threshold
- kernel-selection: add workspace_estimate and frag_penalty to avoid high-workspace kernels on fragmented nodes

Sree: Also implement a shared temp buffer reused across layers for AWQ/GPTQ cast path instead of per-layer ephemeral allocs.

Kai: Perf traces (single-request, seq=8192):
- baseline (old allocator, legacy kernel): peak=19.2GB p99=245ms
- new allocator + latest kernels: peak=21.9GB p99=278ms fragmentation=0.37
- bf16 + conservative kernels: peak=20.1GB p99=275ms

Rachel: Can we determine whether fragmentation is from small-slab holes or large freed blocks not coalesced?

Sam: I instrumented slabpool: free-run counts by bucket. During repro, >64MB buckets increased 3x and there are many 128k/256k holes. So both.

Leo: Action plan (short):
1) fleet experiment to prefer low-workspace kernels for awq/gptq (0.1 rollout)
2) hotfix allocator: trigger eager_compact when deferred_free_len > X or frag_score > 0.25
3) shared-temp-buffer for per-stream reuse (low-risk)

Kai: I'll PR the shared-temp-buffer first (small). Adding reproducer to the PR.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for eng-runtime/canary with kernel-policy-experiment flag. ETA ~20m.

Sree: I'll add metrics: per-node kernel_workspace_pressure gauge and fragmentation alert (pager if p99 > 2x baseline or free_contiguous < 256MB).

Rachel: Also audit FP8->FP16 upcasts for ephemeral buffers. In-place upcast on kv when safe would avoid many allocs.

Sam: Tracking PRs: #4587 shared-temp-buffer, #4588 allocator eager_compact, #4589 kernel frag-penalty. Perf logs attached.

Kai: Quick 1h soak with shared-temp-buffer: zero OOMs, ~600MB transient allocation reduction, p99 stable. I'll open PR now.

Rachel: Nice. Once PRs land we can plan rollout. :party:
